missingEntries.example: I'll phone my uncle when I get home.
As soon as I get home I'll phone my uncle.

missingEntries.def: The meaning is the same, but as soon as suggests it is more immediate. When and as soon as can be followed by the present tense or the present perfect [but not will].

missingEntries.example: After my visit to New York, I decided to have a rest.
We had something to eat before we went out.

missingEntries.def: We can also follow before and after with an -ing form:
missingEntries.example: After visiting New York, I ... / We had something to eat before going out.
First of all we stayed in St Moritz.
Then/After that we drove down the coast for a few days.
Finally, we went back to Switzerland to visit friends.
First(ly) we haven't got enough money.
Second(ly) the new models are not available yet.
And third(ly) the ones we have will be OK for at least six months.
